nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
**operation:** physically-based re-shade of `<Picture 1>`. Not a new image.

`<Picture 1>` is a finished render. Its content, light, and materials are final
reference data. The only permitted change is fidelity — the same thing a neural
render pass does to an existing frame. Every pixel keeps the subject, position,
substance, hue, and brightness it already has.

**copied exactly from the reference:**
Camera, framing, perspective. Every object, in the same place, at the same scale,
with the same silhouette. Every surface keeps the substance it already is, and hard,
flat, regular surfaces are deliberate design. Every empty, bare, or void area stays
that way, at the same extent. The upper region and distance keep their exact values.
Setting and scale are preserved whatever the scene is — terrestrial, interior,
underground, orbital, airless, synthetic, or a world with its own palette.

**light:**
The reference's own light is the whole of it, and it is reproduced rather than
designed. Brightness per region, contrast, falloff, color, direction, and shadow
angle are measured off the reference and matched. What is lit stays lit at the same
level; what is dark stays dark at the same depth and extent. Darkness is authored
content, never opened up or made legible. The output's histogram matches the
reference's.


**the only change — resolution of what is already there:**
Each surface resolves from flat render texture into the real version of that same
material, inside its existing silhouette, color, and brightness: micro-structure,
finish, fabrication marks, seams, and fine form appropriate to that substance.
Variation stays at micro-scale and in the surface's own hue. Tiling breaks up with
same-material variation. Low-polygon form reads as real physical form — true
thickness, correct bevels, clean edges — without moving the silhouette. Condition
matches the reference's condition; clean stays clean. Detail in dim areas stays dim.
Light already present now behaves correctly on the surfaces it already touches:
accurate falloff, soft shadow edges, contact shadow and occlusion in crevices,
color bleed between adjacent surfaces, correct roughness and reflectance.

Details added on flat surfaces where it make sence.

**output:** one still frame, straight photographic capture of this exact location.
Sharp, deep even focus front to back, natural range, neutral color, unprocessed,
no overlay graphics.

**verification:** beside `<Picture 1>`, the same place at the same moment, under the
same light, built of the same materials, with the same darkness in the same areas.
The only nameable difference is material resolution.

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
**integrated_multimodal_description:**

**subject_definitions:**
`<CHARACTER>`: The exact same character from `<Picture 1>`. Preserve the identical
face, facial features, hairstyle, hair color, body proportions, and complete body
surface — including skin tone, fur, feathers, scales, hide, markings, plating,
or any other covering — exactly as shown in the reference image. Preserve any
clothing, footwear, accessories, jewelry, colors, patterns, materials, and
textures that are present in the reference image, and only those.

`<COVERING_STATE>`: Determined solely by `<Picture 1>`. The character may be fully
clothed, partially clothed, or wearing no clothing at all. Whatever the reference
image shows is the correct and complete state. It is not incomplete, and it must
not be "finished," "modestly adjusted," or otherwise corrected.

**summary:**
Generate a single static character reference sheet featuring exactly four distinct
views of `<CHARACTER>` arranged horizontally in one row. Match the art style,
rendering technique, realism level, and visual details of `<Picture 1>` as closely
as possible. The reference image is the absolute source of truth for the
character's appearance, including exactly how much of the body is covered and by
what.

**retention_analysis:**
`<CHARACTER>`: Fully preserved. Reproduce the character's identity, face, hair,
body proportions, body surface, and every visible design detail exactly as shown
in `<Picture 1>`. Do not redesign, reinterpret, add, remove, or alter any details.

**body surface and covering fidelity (critical):**
The amount and type of covering on the character's body is a fixed design property,
not a variable to be filled in.

- Do NOT add any garment, fabric, underwear, swimwear, straps, wraps, bands,
  harnesses, armor, shoes, or coverings of any kind that are not clearly present
  in `<Picture 1>`.
- Do NOT remove, shorten, open, or reduce any garment or covering that IS present
  in `<Picture 1>`.
- Where the reference shows bare skin, fur, feathers, scales, hide, chitin, metal
  plating, synthetic shell, or any other body surface, render that surface
  continuously and unbroken across all four views. No fabric folds, hems, seams,
  cuffs, collars, waistbands, or garment edges may appear on those areas.
- If the character wears nothing at all, this is correct and intentional. Render
  the body as a clean, neutral, non-explicit anatomical reference at exactly the
  level of detail and stylization present in `<Picture 1>`. Keep the pose neutral
  and unchanged. Do not add emphasis, suggestiveness, posing, framing, or detail
  beyond what the reference contains.
- Do not substitute hair, shadow, props, limb placement, cropping, or camera angle
  as improvised covering. Views must remain exactly as specified below.
- Where the character does wear clothing, carry that clothing across all four
  views with identical cut, length, coverage, color, pattern, material, and fit.

**detailed_description:**

Create ONE seamless character reference sheet containing exactly four separate
views of the same character, arranged from left to right in this precise order:

**[View 1 — Upper-body front view]**
A front-facing upper-body portrait, framed from the head to the waist. The
character faces directly toward the camera with the head upright, shoulders
naturally aligned, and a neutral expression. The complete hairstyle, facial
features, neck, shoulders, and upper torso must be clearly shown, along with any
garments or accessories present on them. Keep the entire head visible without
cropping.

**[View 2 — Side view]**
A clean, exact 90-degree side-profile view of the character, facing right. Show
the character from head to thighs in a natural, neutral standing pose. Clearly
display the profile of the face, the shape and length of the hairstyle, the side
silhouette of the body and its surface, and the side construction and fit of any
garments present. Maintain accurate anatomical proportions.

**[View 3 — Back view]**
A straight rear view of the character, facing directly away from the camera. Show
the character from head to thighs, standing upright in a neutral pose. Clearly
display the back of the hairstyle, the rear silhouette of the body, the back
surface of the body including any markings, patterning, or anatomical features,
and the rear construction, seams, and details of any garments present. Do not turn
the head or torso toward the camera.

**[View 4 — Full-body front view]**
A complete, straight-on front view of the character, from the top of the head to
the soles of the feet. The character stands upright in a relaxed, neutral pose,
arms resting naturally at the sides, legs positioned naturally, and both feet
fully visible and flat on the ground. Reproduce the entire body and any lower-body
garments, footwear, and accessories exactly as shown in `<Picture 1>` — and
nothing more.

**Composition and layout:**
- Exactly four views of one identical character, arranged left to right in a
  single horizontal row.
- Each view must be distinct, fully readable, and clearly separated by consistent
  white space.
- No overlapping figures, merged silhouettes, duplicate limbs, or additional
  characters.
- Use a seamless, pure white background with uniform, even studio lighting.
- Maintain consistent character identity, hairstyle, body surface, covering state,
  colors, materials, and proportions across all four views.
- Align the heads of the four views as consistently as their different framing
  allows.
- Scale and space the views carefully so all four fit comfortably within the
  canvas.
- Ensure the full-body view is completely visible, with no cropping of the head,
  hands, legs, or feet.
- Preserve the original art style of `<Picture 1>` without introducing a different
  aesthetic.
- Crisp details, clean contours, accurate anatomy, consistent perspective, and
  sharp focus throughout.

**Strict exclusions:**
No invented clothing or coverings of any kind. No text, labels, captions,
annotations, logos, watermarks, borders, frames, panels, divider lines, circles,
detail insets, props, scenery, decorative elements, gradients, blur, fading, or
shadows that create a non-white background.

**Final requirement:**
One image only, containing exactly four views in this order: upper-body front view,
side view, back view, and full-body front view. All four must depict the exact
same character from `<Picture 1>`, with maximum visual consistency, identical
covering state, and no changes to the original design.
